scenes.tts: A cucumber slice sits overnight in salty water. It gets lighter and goes soft. A slice in plain distilled water gets heavier. Something crossed the edge of the cells, in opposite directions. How does a cell control what gets in and out? And why does salt water make lettuce wilt?
scenes.visual: two beakers with slices (lighter, heavier), then a cell edge with two question-mark arrows and the two questions
scenes.narration: A cucumber slice sits overnight in salty water. It gets lighter and goes soft. A slice in plain distilled water gets heavier. Something crossed the edge of the cells, in opposite directions. How does a cell control what gets in and out? And why does salt water make lettuce wilt?

scenes.tts: Every cell has a cell membrane, a thin boundary around the cell. It is a double layer of fatty molecules called phospholipids, with proteins in it. It is selectively permeable. Some things cross easily, and others hardly at all. Small molecules such as oxygen slip through. Charged ions such as sodium and chloride cross only through proteins.
scenes.visual: membrane as two bars with protein blocks; oxygen passes, ions bounce, then ions pass through proteins
scenes.narration: Every cell has a cell membrane, a thin boundary around the cell. It is a double layer of fatty molecules called phospholipids, with proteins in it. It is selectively permeable. Some things cross easily, and others hardly at all. Small molecules such as oxygen slip through. Charged ions such as sodium and chloride cross only through proteins.

scenes.tts: Passive transport moves a substance from more concentrated to less concentrated. The cell uses no energy. That difference is a concentration gradient. Molecules move at random, so more cross from the crowded side than come back. Diffusion is this spreading out. Facilitated diffusion is diffusion through a membrane protein.
scenes.visual: crowded side, sparse side, high-to-low arrow; dots jiggle and net cross; then dots pass through a protein
scenes.narration: Passive transport moves a substance from more concentrated to less concentrated. The cell uses no energy. That difference is a concentration gradient. Molecules move at random, so more cross from the crowded side than come back. Diffusion is this spreading out. Facilitated diffusion is diffusion through a membrane protein.

scenes.tts: Osmosis is the net movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane. On balance, water moves toward the side with more dissolved solute, because that side has less free water. Saltier outside is hypertonic, and water leaves. Less salty outside is hypotonic, and water enters. Equal is isotonic, and water crosses both ways.

On balance, water moves toward the side with more dissolved solute, because that side has less free water. Saltier outside is hypertonic, and water leaves. scenes.tts: Active transport uses energy from the cell, often from A T P. It can move a substance against its concentration gradient. In animal cells, the sodium potassium pump spends A T P. It moves three sodium ions out and two potassium ions in. Both trips go uphill. Without A T P, the pump stops.

scenes.tts: Now back to the cucumber. The salty water was hypertonic to its cells, so on balance water left them by osmosis. A plant cell has a stiff wall outside its membrane. Water flowing in makes the cell press on the wall. That push is turgor pressure. In salty water the cells lose water and turgor, so the slice goes soft. Lettuce wilts the same way. The membrane chooses what crosses, and water moves toward more solute.
